transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Stocks have extended their rally following Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA as CEO.
Asian markets are advancing after Wall Street surged Monday.
President Trump is taking credit, saying he made the deal.
But while investors are welcoming Huang's return, not everyone is celebrating.
Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen says he believes Trump is motivated by money,
not national security.
"The concern is that it is undermining our national security interests.
After all, high-end ships can be used by the military in China, and it's completely, it's
just completely hypocritical."
Van Hollen is challenging New York Senator Chuck Schumer for the Democratic leaders'
post, and Vidya's board announced Huang's return Monday, less than two weeks after he
resigned amid an alleged Chinese spy scandal.
The Commerce Department, meanwhile, has added to a blacklist Singapore-based MegaSpeed, the
cloud company at the center of the scandal, and also separately added a Singapore subsidiary
of Alibaba.
California Democratic Congressman Jimmy Gomez says he's resigning from Congress after a
bipartisan investigation found substantial evidence that he engaged in sexual misconduct
toward a staffer, NPR's Sam Greenglass reports.
The House Ethics Committee concluded his actions violated House rules by, quote, "making unwelcome
sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome sexual conduct toward a House staffer."
The report also found the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.
Gomez lost reelection this fall and denied the encounters were nonconsensual.
In a statement, he wrote he has strong disagreements with the report and its conclusions.
The committee said Gomez's actions point to a broader culture of disrespect and toxic
sexual behavior toward staff that permeates life on the Hill and is long overdue for correction.
This year, two other House members have also resigned amid sexual misconduct allegations,
and last week, the Ethics Committee unveiled new rules to help speed investigations and
improve transparency.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Washington.
After three Russian missiles fell in its territory last week, Poland asked NATO to strengthen
its share of the country's air defenses.
In Brussels, Terry Schultz reports that the alliance will send Poland an early warning
aircraft.
After NATO ambassadors held an emergency meeting at Poland's request, the alliance's top
military commander, Alexis Grinkowicz, told Poland he would deploy one of the alliance's
shared AWACS aircraft to help the country better defend itself against errant Russian
missiles.
NATO spokesperson Alison Hart says Grinkowicz is also looking at what other assets may be
sent to Poland.
After three Russian ballistic missiles landed in the eastern part of the country Friday
without being intercepted, Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pavel Zilevski says the AWACS plane,
one of 14 NATO has based in Germany, will give Poland better operational awareness to
respond to this kind of threat.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
This is NPR News.
Two Democratic attorneys general are suing several of Elon Musk's companies in connection
with the controversy over his AI chatbot's ability to create sexualized images.
Virginia and Oregon filed suit Monday.
They argue that Musk's companies disregarded safety while building and rolling out the
Grock chatbot.
Several state attorneys general announced investigations in recent months, but Virginia
and Oregon are the first to sue.
Thanksgiving travel shaping up to be messy.
Forecasters warning of a big storm brewing on the east coast.
It could ground the big balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade.
Rainy, windy weather also expected on the west coast.
San Francisco bracing for possible flooding along the waterfront through Thursday.
A group of prominent writers banding together to form a new free speech group called Penn
Rights USA, NPR's Andrew Limbong reports.
Tana Hasikotz, Percival Everett, and Em Gessen are just a few of the big name writers who
are members of Penn Rights USA.
The group is working with a broader free speech group, Penn International, to be recognized
as an official chapter.
Founding member Francine Prose says in a statement that writers have a unique role in promoting
free speech, not just by writing, but "in deciding what an organization like ours stands
for."
Prose is a former president of Penn America, which has gone through a lot of upheaval lately,
particularly over its responses to free speech debates over the war in Gaza.
That org sent a statement to NPR saying it remains committed to protecting free expression
regardless of viewpoints.
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
Again, stocks have extended their rally.
They're up in Asia, advancing after Wall Street surge Monday.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns as NVIDIA CEO; Trump claims credit for deal
Sen. Chris Van Hollen criticizes Trump over NVIDIA chip deal, citing national security concerns
Commerce Department blacklists Singapore-based MegaSpeed and an Alibaba subsidiary
Rep. Jimmy Gomez resigns after House Ethics finding of sexual misconduct toward staffer
NATO to send Poland an AWACS early warning aircraft after Russian missiles landed in Poland
Virginia and Oregon sue Elon Musk's companies over Grok AI sexualized image controversy
Thanksgiving travel forecast messy as major east coast storm threatens Macy's parade balloons
Prominent writers including Tana French and Percival Everett form free speech group Penn Rights USA
Stocks continue rally in Asian markets after Wall Street surge Monday
